criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Mission goal and four quantified requirements cover coverage, resolution, latency and life. Users AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM linked to objectives. Well-referenced rationale for Australian reef benefit.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt Weeks 2-10 with task narrative justifying orbit-before-ground order. Explicit float Week 10 and triggered contingencies including STK loss and coverage shortfall. Sources table maps use. STK choice justified.

evidence.quote: Project work is divided into weeks in the Gantt chart in Figure 1
Week 10 is float as well as editing time

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Hand calcs for 600 km SSO correct for period, orbits/day, 97.8 deg inclination, track shift and 60 km swath. Interpretation identifies weekly coverage risk feeding contingency. STK tutorials plus scenario cross-check show on-track progress.

evidence.quote: Weekly coverage (objective 1) is therefore not guaranteed by one satellite

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings, labelled Figure 1 and Tables 1-3, consistent formatting. Writing clear with good grammar. In-text citations [1]-[11] all match reference list with accessible details.

evidence.quote: Figure 1: Project Gantt chart, Weeks 2 to 10

overall: Strong preliminary report with well-justified reef monitoring mission, robust scheduled plan with contingencies, and correct orbit trade analysis. Meets all Part 1 deliverables to guide full design.

feedback.summary: Well done — you delivered a strong Part 1 with a well-justified reef mission, robust Weeks 2-10 plan with float and contingencies, and correct SSO hand calculations that honestly flag coverage risk. You met all deliverables and are clearly on track for the full design.
next_steps: Carry your four quantified requirements forward and keep them traceable to AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO and BoM needs in the full design.
Protect your Week 10 float and activate your STK-loss and coverage-shortfall contingencies if schedule or analysis slips.
Extend your 600 km SSO hand calculations with STK coverage runs to resolve the weekly revisit gap you identified and size the follow-on design.

criteria.C1: You set a clear reef-monitoring goal with four quantified requirements in Mission Concept & Rationale and linked AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO and BoM to objectives with good references. To secure full marks, keep requirements traceable and deepen literature linkage in the full design.
criteria.C2: You justified your Weeks 2-10 Gantt in Figure 1 with orbit-before-ground sequencing, Week 10 float, triggered contingencies for STK loss/coverage shortfall and a mapped sources table. To secure full marks, keep plan and contingencies aligned to mission narrative as scope evolves.
criteria.C3: You calculated 600 km SSO period, orbits/day, 97.8° inclination, track shift and 60 km swath in Preliminary Progress using T = 2π√(a³/μ) and flagged weekly coverage risk. To secure full marks, expand STK cross-checks and interpret results for constellation sizing.
criteria.C4: You presented clear headings, labelled Figure 1 and Tables 1-3 with consistent formatting and matching [1]-[11] citations. To secure full marks, maintain this consistency, proofread grammar/style, and ensure every figure/table is clearly interpreted in text.
